comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment: City Council Members, I have attended many Meet and Greets for city council candidate in the last 7 years. Jami Leavitt will be an excellent addition. We need consensus builders, excellent communicators, council members who listen well, are approachable, responsive, ethical and knowledgeable about the complex issues St George must successful resolve. Thank you each for your service and I hope you will support the appointment of Jami Leavitt.

comments.subject: Development, Excess
comments.comment:
Well, a new mayor is coming and we wish Mr. Hughes success. I just hope it isn't a continuation of the ruination of St. George by endless development. I guess we just keep doing whatever the developers want. This place is deteriorating so quickly on every front. Water, traffic, the beauty of the surroundings, subdivisions, etc. Time to leave and flee northward. I'm tired of the rubber stamp mentality for the sake of money.

Build it into oblivion……really great….

comments.subject: Fwd: Jr Jazz League
comments.comment:
Greetings,

I've talked to a few basketball boys' parents today and at least four of them are not going to sign their boys up again for Junior Jazz next year. Last year my son's team lost every game lost by at least 35 points EVERY game. This year has started and today at their first game the score was 42 to 9. The team we played against was a full selected team from the league understand what the goal is for St George City in offering this league? I would assume it would be to better the lives of the boys, learn team work, how to work hard, compete well, and this league is structured, it completely deflates full teams of boys, and demoralizes them to where they don't even want to play or finish out the season. I don't want my son competing treated like a high level competitive league, where teams are stacked while other teams have all boys who have never played before. That's what the competitive leagues are for and those already. Even if you created the teams by diving up by geographical area, this would still be better than the current selection process. But clearly the best way to set up the league random selection of players. I have no idea why this isn't the route the city has taken. See attached text thread image of multiple parents discussing the league. Why hasn't the city taken changes so all boys can have a positive experience? I will not be signing my boy up next year if things don't change.

Thank you,
Jodi Gardner
